editorial:
You follow Cole Carter, a 23-year-old DJ chasing a breakthrough track while hanging with his loyal friends in the San Fernando Valley. When older DJ James Reed takes him under his wing, Cole gets a real shot at the big time, but things get messy when he falls for James's girlfriend, Sophie. The movie has a glossy, energetic vibe, mixing club scenes, friendship drama, and romance without feeling too heavy.

The acting is really solid, especially Zac Efron's easy charm and Wes Bentley's worn-out mentor energy, and the music gives the film a strong pulse. The pacing is mostly quick, though some side plots slow things down, and the romance can feel a little thin. Still, it is a fun watch if you like music stories and coming-of-age drama. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Cole finally plays his own track at a big festival instead of just opening for others. The crowd responds, proving he has found his sound. James, who had been distant after learning about Sophie, watches and seems to accept Cole's success. Sophie is there too, but the movie leaves their romance uncertain. Cole's friends are changed by loss and growing up, and Cole walks away knowing he earned his moment.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music stories, friendship drama, and coming-of-age movies.
